tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with the README to understand personal projects and tasks, Markdown, three task views, and local or Telegram account storage. The architecture guide maps the browser, server, synchronization, and operations layers that the following steps connect. The working rules define data-preservation requirements and the boundaries of implemented functionality.

tour.title: Browser Application Composition
tour.description: Following the overview, src/index.js mounts React and registers the offline shell. App composes navigation, dashboard, task views, and account dialogs around shared workspace state rather than letting cards write directly to storage. The HTML template and responsive styles support the same application from narrow mobile screens to desktop.

tour.title: Workspace Model and Mutations
tour.description: The rendered workspace depends on shared normalization, limits, ordering, and compatible snapshot data. Pure mutation functions keep task ownership, protected projects, and pin ordering separate from persistence, while selectors derive the visible dashboard without saving computed state. Read the data guide alongside these widely used modules to understand the contracts later synchronization must preserve.

tour.title: Guarded Edits and Drafts
tour.description: Building on the pure workspace operations, useWorkspace coordinates loading, optimistic quick actions, confirmed saves, and workspace/account action guards. Temporary quick-action previews show pending feedback and roll back on explicit rejection; editing forms retain drafts when confirmation fails. Dialog orchestration and native scroll locking keep these states accessible in the active interface.

tour.title: Task Views and Movement
tour.description: The guarded state feeds dashboard and task-card presentation as well as collapsible Kanban columns. Kanban movement combines pointer and keyboard controls with cancellation, valid destinations, and edge scrolling; overdue tasks may move only to Completed without changing their date. Mouse and touch tests exercise these interaction contracts separately.

tour.title: Safe Content and Language
tour.description: Across those views, shared Markdown rendering constrains links and external images while preserving legacy descriptions. The shared dictionary and language subscriptions provide English and Russian interface and Telegram messages without translating user content. Keeping these policies centralized makes cards, editors, account settings, and bot output consistent.

tour.title: Storage and Offline Synchronization
tour.description: Workspace edits reach persistence through repository selection and the remote repository rather than through individual UI cards. Account-scoped IndexedDB stores durable edits before transmission; revision checks and operation IDs support safe retries after uncertain responses. Field merging preserves separate changes, exposes explicit conflicts, and keeps project navigation device-local.

tour.title: Accounts and Server Persistence
tour.description: The browser synchronization layer talks to authenticated APIs started by the Node.js server. Browser-bound Telegram confirmation establishes the session, and server ownership checks select isolated SQLite workspaces rather than trusting an account identifier inside task data. SQLite transactions retain revisions, operation IDs, sessions, and durable delivery state, while shared validation enforces snapshot limits.

tour.title: Telegram and Account Controls
tour.description: With account ownership established, one Telegram poller handles sign-in confirmation, Inbox capture, language commands, and reminder delivery. The account panel exposes synchronization state, conflict actions, reminder settings, draft export, and guarded logout. The Telegram guide explains how task-form links and durable reminders connect the bot to the same account workspace.

tour.title: Additive Import and Export
tour.description: Import joins the same guarded workspace flow through a validated preview rather than replacing existing data. Templates and legacy backups become fresh copies with new IDs, preserving current projects and merging Inbox tasks into Inbox. Download helpers export JSON locally, and failures leave the preview or original source available for retry.

tour.title: Build and Offline Shell
tour.description: The browser and server behavior rely on the build contract declared by package.json and Webpack. Production bundling applies CSP, extracts styles, and emits a versioned service worker for public application assets. The offline shell supports loading the interface without caching API responses, sessions, or private tasks in Cache Storage.

tour.title: Verification and Safety Evidence
tour.description: Now follow the isolated test setup to see how these contracts are checked with synthetic data and a simulated Telegram backend. Remote browser suites cover account isolation, offline reload, multi-device edits, and explicit conflicts; feedback suites cover pending writes, retained drafts, and rollback. Documentation records the relevant commands and distinguishes completed checks from unverified production behavior.

tour.title: Releases and Recovery
tour.description: Finally, release tooling builds the exact clean pushed commit and verifies the archive checksum and embedded revision before upload or installation. The deployment script locks updates, backs up SQLite, switches release directories, and restores the previous code when health checks fail. The operations guide and backup/restore tools explain recovery separately from application verification; a local build alone does not establish deployment.
